The Brainstem

Brainstem, built on RAPP. Your AI skills, as files you own, that give the same answer every time and go wherever you go.

What it is

The agent: agent.py
One file that does one job. It holds what the skill does, what it needs from you, the steps, and its sample data. Same question in, same answer out, anywhere.
The Brainstem
Anything that runs that file. On your computer it is a chat that loads every file in its agents folder on the next message, using the GitHub Copilot sign-in you already have. Put an agent file beside its one helper, basic_agent.py, and that place is a Brainstem too.

What it promises

  • The whole, not a pile of parts.
    Other tools hand you a model, a harness, a loop, skill files and connectors, and you become the glue. An agent file is all of it in one; the Brainstem is the loop.
  • Same answer, every time.
    The steps are code, not instructions an AI re-reads and re-interprets. Anyone can re-run it and check.
  • Your work comes back out.
    Getting an agent into one platform is easy. Getting it out again, into whatever comes next, is the hard part. The file is the original; every platform version is made from it.
  • Yours, on your machine.
    No cloud to set up, no keys, no admin. Plain files you can open, share and keep.
  • Built to grow into a swarm.
    Agents follow the rapp/1 standard: the same agent is the same bytes everywhere, and the platform grows by adding agents, never new connections. Many Brainstems can share agents and check each other's answers.

The shape is the brand

A Brainstem is recognised by its shape, not by where it runs: an agent.py, its basic_agent.py, and a chat that answers with them. If it looks like a Brainstem and answers like a Brainstem, it is a Brainstem. That is why anyone can stand one up wherever they need it, with whatever they have.

Graduation: your whole Brainstem, every tier

Graduation is the Brainstem's launch pipeline. Whatever you have loaded into your Brainstem, its agents, its instructions and what it remembers, graduates together as one brain. It is part of the Brainstem, not a separate tool.

  • Tier 1, Brainstem: the brain runs on your computer, as you built it.
  • Tier 2, Spinal Cord (Azure): the same brain runs in the cloud.
  • Tier 3, Nervous System (Microsoft 365): the brain's agents are rebuilt as Copilot Studio and Power Platform parts, and every rebuilt step is checked against the agent's own answers before it ships. A step that does not match is not shipped.

At every tier the test is the same: same question, same answer as your Brainstem.

Any AI is the plug

The Brainstem is not a second boss. The AI you already use plugs into it and gets more reach: your computer, your skills and your memory. Your AI stays in charge, under its own rules.

Your AI stays home

Skills and memory are plain files on your computer that you own and can read. Change which AI you use and you lose nothing; the next one plugs into the same Brainstem.

Voice first

The Brainstem is built to be spoken to. Say "R-A-P-P" (spelled out) or "Brainstem" and it starts listening, for any command.

The rare names are on purpose. A common word comes up in everyday talk, so an assistant named with one keeps waking by mistake or misses its name. Nobody says "R-A-P-P" or "Brainstem" by accident, so it wakes only when you mean it.

Answers come back short and easy to say out loud. The people around you hear what you are working on, not just the sound of typing.

How we talk about it

The full name is Brainstem, built on RAPP. Brainstem is the product people use; RAPP is the open pattern it is built on (agent.py files and one chat). Say "RAPP" spelled out, R-A-P-P.

Hard questions

Short answers for skeptical rooms.

  • Isn't my AI enough on its own? On its own it forgets what it built. The Brainstem keeps each skill as a file, so it is built once and every AI can use it.
  • Is it safe? It works with the access you give it, under the rules of the AI you already use. If you want less, run it in a container; it does less, and that is your choice.
  • Where does my data go? Nowhere new. It stays as files on your computer.
  • What if I switch AIs? Nothing is lost. Skills and memory stay put.
  • What does it cost? It runs on your existing GitHub Copilot sign-in. There is no separate bill.

Why it stays

Today one package offers all of this together, and it is the Brainstem. It stays until someone else builds the same thing. We check every month and record what we find.
